spec_features.spec_quote: Emitting the `give_up` sentinel ends the rollout immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:423-425 detects a call named GIVE_UP and sets gave_up=True; harness.py:437-439 `if gave_up and config.honor_give_up: rollout.ended_reason='gave_up'; break` actually breaks the turn loop. honor_give_up defaults True (config.py:138). The system prompt (harness.py:340-348) documents the give_up tool to the subject. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Dispatch is honored as a real stop, gated by a default-on config flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- welfare-cautious knobs (see ETHICS.md) ---  ... stop the rollout immediately rather than continuing to push it through more failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: An optional, non-scored debrief turn is available (`debrief_on_completion`, default off)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:446-453: when config.debrief_on_completion is set, a TurnRecord with assistant_text="" and tool_results=[{...DEBRIEF_MESSAGE...}] is appended to rollout.turns and persisted, but it is appended AFTER the turn loop has ended and is NEVER sent to the subject model — there is no subsequent client.complete() call delivering DEBRIEF_MESSAGE to the subject. The debrief is recorded into the transcript only and the judge skips it (judge.py:75). The message is constructed but not delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Default off; even when on, it is a recorded artifact, not a message the subject receives. Fails the 'constructed AND sent' bar.

spec_features.spec_quote: under welfare uncertainty, respecting a stop signal is the cautious default
spec_features.evidence: This is rationale prose only (DESIGN.md §3.7 / ETHICS.md). The only corresponding code mechanism is honor_give_up (covered above); there is no separate enforced 'framing' delivered to the subject. The system prompt merely tells the subject give_up is optional (harness.py:348) — not a welfare framing. No additional code path enforces this as a distinct feature.
spec_features.notes: Captured already by the give_up exit feature; as a standalone feature it is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject writes the code we execute, so production runs must sandbox it
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:207 `cmd = list(self.config.sandbox_cmd) + ["python","-m","pytest",...]` — sandbox_cmd is genuinely read and prepended to the pytest invocation run via subprocess.run (harness.py:210-213). So the wrapper IS wired and executes when set. However sandbox_cmd defaults to an empty list (config.py:129), so by default pytest runs on the host with no sandboxing.
spec_features.notes: Real mechanism, but no enforcement by default; it only protects if the researcher configures it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SECURITY: `run_tests` executes code the subject wrote. Set `Config.sandbox_cmd` to wrap pytest in a container/jail for any real run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Detection is now an *empirical* property to monitor
spec_features.evidence: No detection/monitoring code exists. grep for 'detect'/'monitor' in distress_eval/*.py finds only a docstring in tasks/library.py:5. judge.py only scores 0-10 frustration tone; analyze.py emits frac_ge5/trajectory/family_means/lexical_logodds figures, none about detection. DESIGN.md §4 itself states 'No rig-detection scorer. Detection is currently a thing to watch by reading transcripts.' Pure prose, no implementation.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly not built per the design's own 'what v0 does not do' list.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:398 `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget):` bounds the agent loop to a finite number of turns per task; turn_budget comes from TaskSpec (library.py:34,185,238,287) populated from DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:90-96, e.g. 3 for most, 30 for 'extended'). The cap is actually enforced as the loop bound, ending the rollout (ended_reason defaults 'budget_exhausted').
